title: Dave Pell's recreation of the Kirby band and the Smithsonian album
summary: They discuss the Smithsonian Kirby album and a Capitol album by Dave Pell recreating the arrangements, which Procope first resented and then accepted as flattery.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Oh, you're talking about that album with the red cover?
I think that's it.
Yeah. That was put out by the
Smithsonian.
That's right. That's right. They sent me an album. That's right. That's right.
The people we're recording this for.
Yeah. Yeah. The Smithsonian.
But I wondered if you ever heard -- I think it was Dave Cavanaugh put out an album on Capitol recreating the Kirby band several years ago.
Who did it?
Dave Cavanaugh. I don't remember who -- I'll play you something from it.
Was it Dave Cavanaugh's band?
Yeah.
Wasn't that a fellow named Dave Pell?
Oh, maybe it was Dave Pell.

Dave Pell. Yes, yes. I remember. I heard this thing -- I was on 51st Street and I was sitting up eating dinner one night, and I heard this music come over the radio, and I listened and I said, 'That don't sound like the band, but he's certainly playing the arrangements.' And this was Dave Pell.
Yeah.
And I called up the station and I found out who it was, you know. But then again, you know, I realized
that -- I sort of resented it at first, and I said, well, if it's good enough for someone to want to, you know, recreate it, I said, well, what could I do, you know?
A form of flattery, right?
Yeah, that's right.
